record.identity: (encounter_id, run_key); encounter_id is a deterministic function of the spec, run_key of the execution, so several run_keys under one encounter_id are REPLAYS of one spec
fields_it_does_not_carry: any score or metric (scores live on SFE observations, reached through sfe_entry_hash)
record.consequence: the encounter record answers questions about OUTCOME TOKENS, FAILURE CLASSES, RESOURCES, REPLAY IDENTITY, PROVENANCE COVERAGE and LINEAGE EDGES. It cannot answer a performance question (no metric) or a causal one (no intervention): HA-1.1, HA-1.2. Every manifest below is bounded accordingly.

common.source_refs_form: an ORDERED list of (encounter_id, run_key, sfe_entry_hash, revision) enumerated by a read whose filter (namespace = prod, occurred_ts window, world set) is written into the manifest addendum BEFORE the statistic; the list, not the filter, is the source
common.source_set_digest: sha256 over the canonicalised, sorted source_refs, computed by the addendum
common.mode: FROZEN for each manifest below: this file's commit precedes any read for these questions; EXPLORATORY output from earlier ad-hoc reads (none on record for these questions at 2026-09-18) is never relabelled
common.exclusions_rule: namespace <> 'prod' (fixtures) excluded and COUNTED; rows whose sfe_entry_hash does not resolve on the SFE ledger excluded and COUNTED as UNANCHORED; the rule is identical across every group compared
common.replay_rule: run_keys under one encounter_id are ONE unit (QR-REPLAY; replay_attestation); the unit count is the count of distinct encounter_ids after exclusions

manifests.question: Is an encounter spec deterministic across executions? (replay identity)

unit_of_analysis.declared_n: count of such encounter_ids after exclusions
unit_of_analysis.mapping_rule: group source_refs by encounter_id; a group of size 1 is ineligible for this question and is counted, not dropped silently

measurement_identity.definition: IDENTICAL iff every run_key of the encounter_id carries the same outcome token AND the same resources_used JSON (canonicalised)

declared_null.generator: none needed: the statistic is a count of exact identities
declared_null.attainable_range: fraction in [0, 1]; the interval is a Clopper-Pearson binomial on n eligible encounter_ids

controls.positive: fixture pairs (namespace test) with identical bytes read IDENTICAL
controls.negative: a fixture pair with a perturbed resources_used reads DIVERGENT
controls.cheat: a pair whose run_keys are the same string is REFUSED as a replay (one execution, two rows)

manifests.min_attainable_p: not a hypothesis test; interval only; n < 1 -> NOTHING_COULD_FIRE
manifests.exclusions: common rule; groups of size 1 listed as INELIGIBLE with their count
manifests.reading_bound: a DIVERGENT fraction > 0 is a finding about the executor (nondeterminism or a leaked run-specific input), never about the world; it feeds QR-REPLAY, which then refuses those rows as attestations

manifests.question: What is the outcome-token distribution per world and per player, and does it change across occurred_ts? (descriptive; no causal reading)

unit_of_analysis.unit: the distinct encounter_id (replays collapsed to one row by PEW-E1's rule, the FIRST run_key in revision order)
unit_of_analysis.declared_n: distinct encounter_ids after exclusions, per (world_id) and per (player)
unit_of_analysis.mapping_rule: one row per encounter_id; a multi-player encounter contributes to each of its players' tables and the double-counting is printed

measurement_identity.range: the native token vocabulary, enumerated from the rows and printed
measurement_identity.definition: counts per token; failure_class cross-tabulated within the failure tokens

declared_null.generator: token labels permuted across encounter_ids within a world (exchangeable-in-time null); the time-change statistic is the chi-square over occurred_ts quartiles
declared_null.attainable_range: chi-square in [0, inf); with k tokens and 4 quartiles the lattice minimum p is printed from the permutation count

controls.positive: a synthetic world whose token mix flips at its median timestamp must fire
controls.negative: a permuted copy must not fire above alpha
controls.cheat: a world with one token everywhere is a structural floor (floor_precheck p_mode = 1.0) and is REFUSED, not reported as 'no change'

manifests.eligible_count: worlds with >= 8 distinct encounter_ids AND >= 2 tokens in support; printed before any chi-square
manifests.min_attainable_p: from the permutation lattice at the eligible n; worlds below alpha-attainability are NOTHING_COULD_FIRE
manifests.exclusions: common rule; worlds failing floor_precheck listed with p_mode
manifests.reading_bound: HA-1.1 / HA-1.2: a time-change in token mix is an ASSOCIATION with time; it names no cause and licenses no performance claim. Rows within a world are ordered by occurred_ts, so the exchangeability diagnostic (EX-1.0.0) is printed per world and a VIOLATED world's permutation p is not quoted

manifests.question: Is resource use (resources_used.*) associated with outcome token, within a world?

measurement_identity.range: [0, inf) per key; keys enumerated from the rows and each analysed SEPARATELY, never pooled (X1-b)
measurement_identity.definition: per key, the distribution of the value by outcome token

declared_null.generator: outcome labels permuted within the world (Mann-Whitney / Kruskal on the resource value)
declared_null.attainable_range: U statistic lattice; minimum p from the group sizes, printed

controls.positive: a synthetic world where failures cost 2x must fire
controls.cheat: a resources_used key that is a deterministic function of the outcome token (e.g. a 'failed_at_tick' present only on failures) is detected by a presence-by-token table and REFUSED as an analysis of association

manifests.eligible_count: worlds with >= 8 encounter_ids per compared token; printed first
manifests.min_attainable_p: from the rank lattice at the eligible group sizes
manifests.exclusions: common rule; encounters with resources_used = null listed and counted
manifests.reading_bound: association within a world; resource use is not an intervention here (budget is declared per encounter, not assigned by an experimenter); any 'cost of failure' sentence is descriptive

manifests.question: What fraction of encounters is anchor-verifiable (STRICT provenance with a resolvable sfe_entry_hash), per engine instance and over time?

unit_of_analysis.unit: the (encounter_id, run_key) row -- every execution's provenance is its own fact
unit_of_analysis.mapping_rule: no collapsing: a replay with a different engine instance is a different provenance row

measurement_identity.definition: fraction with sfe_affinity_mode = STRICT AND sfe_entry_hash resolving on the ledger named by sfe_engine_instance_id (verify_anchor), per engine instance and per occurred_ts month

controls.positive: a fixture row with a known-good anchor resolves
controls.negative: a fixture row with a fabricated hash does NOT resolve and is counted UNANCHORED
controls.cheat: a row whose sfe_entry_hash resolves on a DIFFERENT engine instance than its sfe_engine_instance_id names is counted MIS-ANCHORED, never verified

manifests.eligible_count: rows per engine instance; printed first
manifests.exclusions: namespace <> prod only; nothing else is excluded because unanchored rows are the object
manifests.reading_bound: this is the eligibility denominator for every other manifest in this family: PEW-E1..E3, E5 run on the anchor-verifiable subset, and the fraction here is printed beside their results

manifests.question: Do lineage edges (ew.fossil_edges: SURVIVAL / EXTINCTION / TRANSFER / ...) associate with encounter outcome tokens for the same player?

unit_of_analysis.declared_n: players with >= 1 edge AND >= 8 distinct encounter_ids
unit_of_analysis.mapping_rule: join fossil_edges.src_id = player to encounters where player = ANY(players); a player's encounters are within-unit repeats

measurement_identity.definition: per player: relation counts and outcome-token counts; the association statistic is over PLAYERS (unit), not over encounters

declared_null.attainable_range: from the permutation lattice at n_players

controls.positive: a synthetic lineage where EXTINCTION follows a run of failure tokens must fire
controls.cheat: an edge whose sfe_entry_hash equals an encounter's sfe_entry_hash is the SAME event recorded twice, and the pair is collapsed before counting (else the association is with itself)

manifests.eligible_count: n_players meeting the mapping rule; printed first
manifests.min_attainable_p: 2 / permutation count at n_players; below alpha-attainability -> NOTHING_COULD_FIRE
manifests.exclusions: common rule; edges with no sfe_entry_hash listed as UNANCHORED and counted
manifests.reading_bound: HA-1.2: an association between lineage events and outcome tokens; the direction of cause is not in the record

not_declared_because_the_record_cannot_a: any question of the form 'which player performs better' (no metric on the record; go through sfe_entry_hash to the observation and declare an SFE analysis under WP-X1)
any question of the form 'does X cause Y' (no intervention field; HA-1.2)
any question about ecology or budget effects (declared inputs, not assigned treatments; an association manifest may be added as PEW-E6 when a question is actually asked)
consumers: Mnemosyne (PEW owner) may run E1 and E4 as substrate validation; Archaeon may run E2/E3/E5 on the anchor-verifiable subset; each run binds source_refs by addendum first
